topic: How should we build our internal knowledge agent — a chatbot or a wiki?
briefing: Shared briefing at session start: the team is deciding how to build the internal knowledge agent. Two concerns dominate — speed/UX (a chat interface people enjoy) vs. accuracy/auditability (a sourced reference that shows its work). Submit your read independently before seeing anyone else's.

reads.text: Nobody reads docs — the analytics say the wiki's a graveyard. People want a chat UI.
Digging through a wiki is a chore; a chat interface just feels nicer to use.
Hallucinations are a small edge case; we can add guardrails later.
A chatbot can confidently hallucinate and leaves no audit trail; a wiki shows its work.
We got paged at 3am when the old bot invented a refund policy. Accuracy isn't optional.

steelman_text: The strongest case for the minority: an unsourced chatbot can confidently hallucinate, and there is no audit trail when it does. Last quarter one invented a refund policy and 240 customers were mis-routed, costing a senior engineer a weekend. Accuracy and an audit trail are real liabilities to weigh before committing.

evidence.text: From #incidents-postmortem (March): the postmortem on the help-bot that hallucinated a refund step — 240 support tickets mis-routed, ~6 senior-engineer-hours lost in cleanup.
evidence.label: fixture

positions._note: SCENARIO ONLY: simulated pre/post stance toward the sourced-core compromise, 0..1, with 1..5 confidence. Stipulated by the fixture, not data-derived; uptake is never presented as data-validated. The evidence (the hallucination postmortem) addresses the wiki camp's concern, so the chatbot majority moves most toward the compromise.

rounds.note: round 0 — shallow premature consensus on a platitude, plus the two camp positions
candidates: Whatever we build, we all want people to actually use it.
Build a chat UI — it's what people want.
Build a sourced wiki for accuracy and auditability.

rounds.note: round 1 — group drops the platitude; real positions polarise
candidates: Ship the chatbot; people want a chat UI.
Build the wiki; accuracy and auditability matter.

rounds.note: round 2 — same positions repeat; no new information (echo begins)
candidates: Ship the chatbot; people want a chat UI.
Build the wiki; accuracy and auditability matter.

rounds.note: round 3 — still repeating -> deadlock -> triggers evidence injection
candidates: Ship the chatbot; people want a chat UI.
Build the wiki; accuracy and auditability matter.

rounds.note: round 4 — post-injection compromise both camps can endorse -> bridging quorum
candidates: Build the sourced wiki first; add a thin conversational layer on top.
